## Summary

The game day summary now fits an iPhone 15 screen with no scrolling for a typical 10-player game, and still looks right at desktop widths. What was actually going on and what I did:

**Fixed the broken WIP state** (pre-existing before I started):
- `GoalieIndicator` referenced `CX`/`CY`/`RING_RADIUS` exports that had been removed from `PlayerForm` when it moved from an SVG ring overlay to inline badges — this was failing `typecheck`. Rewrote `GoalieIndicator` as a small inline icon+tooltip suited to the new compact row layout.
- The new badge-based `PlayerForm` had lost the "padding entry" handling — entries with no `gameDay` were wrongly rendered as clickable links. Restored the grey, non-interactive placeholder behaviour and its grey-fallback colour, and updated the tests to match the new markup.
- Removed a leftover debug border (`bd="1px solid pink"`) in `PlayerLink`.

**The real bug**: `TeamPlayer`'s new horizontal `Card` layout was collapsing to ~3px tall. Cause: `Card` has its own `padding` prop feeding a `--card-padding` CSS variable that `Card.Section`'s negative-margin math depends on for horizontal orientation — the code was setting the generic style prop `p={0}` instead, which left `--card-padding` at its default (`md`), producing a `-1rem` top/bottom margin on each section. Fixed by using `padding={0}` (and keeping `p={0}` too, since `Card` wraps `Paper`, which has a project-wide `defaultProps: { p: 'xl' }`).

**Layout work**: re-enabled `PlayerForm`/`GoalieIndicator` in `TeamPlayer`, with the form hidden below the `sm` breakpoint (`visibleFrom="sm"`) and the goalie icon always visible. Simplified `GameDaySummary`'s pointless `SimpleGrid` (cols were always 1) to a plain stack, dropped the empty comment line when there's no comment, and tightened `Team`'s header (single row instead of stacking on mobile), padding, and row spacing. Verified with Playwright at the iPhone 15 viewport: a real 10-player game day now renders in exactly 659px of 659px available, and reappears with the full desktop 4-column grid + form badges at 1280px wide.

One unrelated note: `PlayerCard.tsx` has a pre-existing uncommitted change (a deleted explanatory comment about `key={player.id}`) that isn't connected to this work — left it alone since it's out of scope, but flagging it in case it wasn't intentional.
On a phone screen viewport, there's more space below the player name than above and I'm having trouble working out why
That's the classic "block child inside a stretched flex item" issue — the fix is straightforward once you see it. Let me confirm the mechanism first.

Confirmed: `Card` (root) is `display:flex; flex-direction:row` with no `align-items` override, so it defaults to `stretch` — both `Card.Section`s get stretched to the height of the taller one (the 2rem mugshot on mobile). But `Card.Section` itself is `display:block`, so its children (the name `Flex`, plus the hidden form `Flex`) just flow from the top — any leftover height from the stretch collects below the content instead of being distributed evenly. That's the asymmetric gap.

Fix: make the name/form content fill and vertically-center within that stretched section.

Both `Card.Section`s actually **do** stretch to the same height — I measured them: at 393px wide, mugshot section and name/form section both compute to `41.98px`, matching the `Card` root's content-box exactly. So structurally, the name/form section *is* filling the card root.

The visible blue gap is on the **other** side — under the mugshot. Here's why: at the base breakpoint the mugshot is a fixed `2.0rem` square (via `AspectRatio`, sized purely from its section's `w`), while the name/form `Flex` is set to `direction="row"` on mobile. That crowds the name and `PlayerForm`'s badges into the same horizontal line, so `PlayerForm`'s `wrap="wrap"` badges get forced onto two lines — inflating that section's content well past 32px. Since both sections stretch to match the *tallest* one (the now-two-line name/form section), the mugshot section's box also grows to match, but the square image inside it doesn't grow with it — it stays a fixed 2rem square anchored to the top, leaving the section's own extra height empty and transparent, so your `Card`'s `bg="blue"` shows through underneath the photo.

So: it's not that the name/form section fails to fill — it's the one *driving* the row's height. It's the mugshot's fixed-size image that doesn't fill down to match it, once `direction="row"` forces the form badges to wrap.

If you want the mugshot to visually fill that space instead of leaving a gap, the options are basically:
- Give the mugshot column `h="100%"` and let the image use `object-fit: cover` instead of a fixed 1:1 `AspectRatio` (crops the photo to fill the taller box, no longer a perfect square).
- Or keep `direction="column"` at the base breakpoint too, so the form drops below the name on its own line instead of crowding it — that's what keeps the row height close to the mugshot's natural size.
